# BOOK 1 of 2: THE GHOST OF MYSTERY AIRPORT (Van Powell, 1932, Saalfield)

## Cast (key)
- **Garry (Garfield) Duncan**, 15, student-pilot, practical, calm, humorous; knows aircraft design from blueprint room.
- **Chick (Chickering) Brown**, 13, impulsive, timid at first, brave later, philatelist (stamp collector), kindly.
- **Don McLeod**, 17, pilot, nephew of **Bruce McLeod** (airport manager/designer, harassed, invested savings). Flies **Dragonfly** (3-seat biplane amphibian, white wings, Gossport tube) and **Dart** (light fast 2-seat, red wings, owned by McLeod).
- **Scott ("Great Scott")**, test pilot, chief hangar supervisor, "likes spooks"; secretly the villain. Limps after "prop" injury (faked). Leg bandaged.
- **Doc Morgan**, airport handyman, herb "doctor," drinks, nickname; wears bandage on head in boathouse; innocent.
- **Toby Tew**, boatman (dories) and picture-palace manager (the Palace), kindly; has boathouse with trapdoor.
- **John C. Vance / "J. V."**, control-room chief, initials on tracing; (cleared).
- **Ti-O-Ga**, old Indian medicine man, Catskills; **John Tioga**, his son (ex-navy cadet training, Carlisle school, film extra in "Red Blood and Blue").
- **Chief of Police** (unnamed); postal inspector (unnamed).
- Mail pilot **Smith** (Philadelphia run) — used as cover identity by Scott.
- Clam-digger **old Ike** (source of 1-old crack-up legend).
- Mail 'plane pilot who crashed first (story of "spectre").
- Liner **Caledonia** (mail from Liverpool).

## Plot events in order
1. July night, Garry, Chick and Scott fly the Dragonfly over Long Island marsh (Port Washington, Mystery Airport) to catch "Sky Spook." Scott claims spook appears every 7th day, 4 weeks; name "Mystery Airport" from newspapers. Scott says ghost haunts clouds; Garry thinks human. Engine "cut" — dead-stick glide. Chick frightened.
2. Don arrives in Dart (flown with Scott's plan). Old Ike's story: two planes collided over Devil's Sink; skeleton found there. Scott's theory: guilty ghost haunts place. Airlane Guard formed.
3. Don flies Dragonfly; Scott in Dart. Spectre seen in cloud; mail 'plane (Dragonfly area) crashes into bay; phantom planes collide, no crash heard. Flare shows pilot's crash; mail 'plane tangled in marsh.
4. Storm. Dragonfly lands at old boathouse dock; Chick ties ship, goes into shack, finds **Doc Morgan** drunk, with tracing paper (sketch of "all-metal ship"). Chick flees; "Thing That Never Was / Man Who Never Lived" (green oilskins, rubber cap/gloves) grabs him; Chick keeps tracing; loses stamp envelope.
5. Don and Garry row dory to mail 'plane; Garry gets mail pouch; pilot found (injured man, runs/crumples). Chick missing. Don flies Dragonfly (pilot and mail) above storm; Garry repairs cut elevator cables by hand. Land at farm near Catskill.
6. Farmer; **Ti-O-Ga** arrives in Ford; sets pilot's arm; hypnotizes Garry in his cottage (daughter "not altogether Indian"); gives **pouch charm** ("to clip ghost wings"), wear 7 days then open.
7. Mail delivered; Chick tells story; Vance claims tracing is his lost sketch (initials J.V.). Don offers to fly mail; Dragonfly flies to meet liner Caledonia; Chick and Garry catch mail buoy. Helicopter seen over swamp. Helicopter attacks with rockets; Don does barrel rolls, falling leaf, lands at runway. Don takes Dart back; Garry takes crash launch; Demon in helicopter by Crab Channel.
8. Garry on launch, spotlight; Don spots Demon, Indian (John) turns out to be pilot; Demon (Scott disguise) escapes, Indian John captured. (Chick and Vance paths.)
9. Morning: Chief? no—McLeod takes them through swamp; John Tioga confesses: father's pirate-brig map from dying sailor; Doc Morgan phoned John about mail pilot; Ti's "charm" passes = theater passes; three yellow "Palace" passes.
10. Palace show: smoke projection on cloud (Tew suspected). Chick develops film; Doc found in darkroom; tear-gas smoke bomb; film stolen. Chase; Dragonfly & Dart chase; John flies Dart; Scott's mail 'plane fight; Scott crashes and dies. Ghost ended.

Key devices: smoke-cloud projector; helicopter with calcium light (oxygen tank), film of swamp; map camouflaged as airplane tracing (brig hull, Crab Channel, boathouse channel = treasure "Lady O' Fortune"/chest). Chest never recovered; Scott's ruse: bought skeleton from hospital to start search far from real spot.

# BOOK 2 of 2: LOVE AND THE IRONMONGER (F. J. Randall, 1908, John Lane)

## Setup
- Firm: **Fairbrother and Co.**, iron merchants, Upper Thames Street; warehouse "Iron Wharf."
- **Old Joseph (Joe) Fairbrother** (head) dies; legacies of £500/yr each to three staff on conditions of reform:
  - **Thomas Parrott**, head clerk; mean → must lend on request.
  - **Albert Busby**, cashier; liar → must tell truth (wife Fanny, Clapham, Sunday school hobby).
  - **Jimmy Gray**, accountant; drinker (Leytonstone villa, wife **Emily/Em**). Later secretary of "Old Friends' Society" (Lambert).
- Condition: three warnings → loss of legacy; loss passes to "husband" of Miss Fairbrother if she marries; otherwise to charities ("Very Dark African Mission").
- Narrator: **George Early**, junior clerk, ambitious; lodger at Mrs. Haskins' (Carrie maid) initially; later lodges with Gray in Leytonstone (Mrs. Gray).
- Early chapters: George overhears interviews through keyhole (hides in box-room). Gets half-crown from Parrott; blackmails each; swears to fit legacies.
- Ch. III: Miss **Ellen Fairbrother** (Australia, 22) assumes control; lives Brunswick Terrace, Kensington/West End, with aunt **Aunt Phoebe**. George blackmails Parrott (borrowing), Gray (£5 for secret of Busby), Busby (lies to wife about Free Library).
- Ch. IV–V: Gray; "Old Josh" (Benson) loan; Parrott dismisses George; George wins promotion.
- Ch. VI: Parrott hides in cupboard while George dines with **Lucy Perkins** (Parrott's fiancée, milliner, Paddington; mother Mrs. Perkins). Lamb chops, claret. George asks Parrott to borrow £10 — Parrott's hoard.
- Ch. VII: George secretary to Ellen; Mrs. Gray & Mrs. Busby (bookshelf rivalry at Stratford).
- Ch. VIII: George rescues Ellen from hansom in Regent Street; Gray pays £5 for George's knowledge of Busby's vices; Busby/George smoking concert; George swaps vices.
- Ch. IX: conspiracy against George; Ellen's letter promotes George to acting head.
- Ch. X–XII: Ellen–George courtship (Hampton Court boat trip), engagement. Cacklin and Billy Budd (office boys) gossip.
- Ch. XIII: Wedding; Aunt Phoebe interviews George. Gray & Mrs Gray's drink; Mole (lawyer's clerk, detective of Dibbs & Dubbs) tricks Gray with "Tommy Morgan" whisky.
- Ch. XIV–XV: George now head of firm; Dibbs & Dubbs (lawyers, St Paul's Passage) under new partner Dawkins; Gray's first warning; if Gray loses, legacy reverts to George; if George loses, Ellen's fortune goes to charity — George: "SILLY OLD FOOL!"
- Ch. XVI–XVII: George tries teetotal; Gray's second warning; Mrs. Early. Gray gets legacies by blackmail; George's Sunday-school decorations.
- Ch. XVIII–XX: Gray & co. blackmail Dawkins; George tricked by hypnotist Caroli (foreign customer) into drinking whisky → third warning.
- Ch. XXI–XXII: George escapes to Wheatsheaf Inn (country), disguises; Gray/Busby/Parrott trace him; fire-alarm in cloak-room; chase up oak tree; falls; "deaf and blind"; Dr **John Cattermole** (Walworth chemist, friend) rescues him; Hastings; George pretends to be lost son "Erny" of landlady ("Moggles"); swaps clothes with son Albert; escapes to London.
- Ch. XXIV: Ellen's cousin "Tops" (Miss Fairbrother's cousin, daughter of John Fairbrother) arrives; strawberry birthmark reveals Mrs. Early (Ellen, "Babs") is actually John's daughter?—Resolved: wife Ellen = Babs, cousin Tops is heiress (actual Miss Fairbrother, daughter of John), wife's Brixton house.
- Ch. XXV (end): George has lost fortune to cousin "Tops"; Cattermole says George now manager of firm under her; baby "Phoebe" joke. Three men reinstated. Ends.

Other notes: Old Joe lawyers "Dibbs and Dubbs." Warehouse: Iron Wharf. Firm's motto items: stoves ("Little Wonder," "Little Midget"), pamphlet claims. Dinner: rabbit (Mrs. Haskins).
